what: What did each Lunenburg town employee earn in 1984?
why: `report-gross-wages` holds per-employee earnings from the 1995-2010 reports and FY2011-FY2025. The 1984 annual town report prints no wage list: the whole text (146 pages) was searched for wage, gross, salary and payroll and found only the Treasurer's payroll DEDUCTION totals (p42, p45), the Auditor's note that he reviewed payroll time sheets (p8), `Special Detail Wages` (p43, p44) and the school staff biographies (p122-133), which give position and credentials and no pay (sources/data/report-tables/1984/). — closes: the Town's calendar-1984 payroll register (W-2 totals by employee) from the Treasurer's office.

what: What were the town's non-union salary grades and step rates in fiscal 1985?
why: `salary-schedule` and `report-classification-plan` read Schedule A from the 2010 report and FY2011 onward. The 1984 annual town report prints only the articles that replaced the Classification and Salary Schedule (p74 Article 2 for the May 12, 1984 meeting; p86 Article 1 for November 1, 1984) and one amended excerpt, the Trades and Services and Recreation rates (p86, not landed: NEEDS.md); searched for classification, salary schedule, step and grade (sources/data/report-tables/1984/). — closes: the Personnel Committee's Classification and Salary Schedule as it appeared in the Finance Committee report to the May 12, 1984 Annual Town Meeting.

what: What did each special revenue fund take in, spend and carry forward in fiscal 1984, town-wide?
why: `special-revenue-funds` holds forward, receipts, disbursements and balance by fund from the 1995-2010 reports. The 1984 report prints the revolving funds' YEAR-END balances only, as lines of the balance sheet (p46 `Other Revolving Funds`) and the School Department's own special accounts with balance on hand, receipts and expenditures (p139-142, landed as `report-school-special-accounts`); no town-wide schedule with a forward, receipts, disbursements and balance by fund. Searched revolving and special revenue (sources/data/report-tables/1984/). — closes: the Town Accountant's fiscal 1984 special revenue fund ledger.

what: What was appropriated, spent and carried forward on each capital project fund in fiscal 1984?
why: `report-capital-projects` holds a capital project fund schedule from the 2001-2010 reports. The 1984 report prints no such schedule: the balance sheet carries `Appropriation for Capital Improvements` as one reserve with its projects listed (p47) and the accountant's schedule (p53-59) carries the same projects as articles. Searched capital project and capital improvement (sources/data/report-tables/1984/). — closes: the Town Accountant's fiscal 1984 capital projects fund ledger.

what: What did each item of Lunenburg's FY1985 capital plan cost?
why: `capital-plans` holds item-by-item costs. The 1984 report prints no capital plan: the only mentions are the School Committee's budget priorities in prose (p95: $70,000 for the high school roof, $31,000 for a wheelchair lift). Searched capital plan and capital improvement (sources/data/report-tables/1984/). — closes: the Finance Committee's FY1985 report listing the capital articles.

what: What was Lunenburg's assessed valuation by property class, its levy, overlay and new growth for fiscal 1985?
why: `report-valuation` holds the Assessors' tables (assessments by class, valuation and tax history, abstract by class code, overlay, new growth) from the 1995-2010 reports. The 1984 report prints the valuation in prose only: real estate $190,229,912 and personal property $6,301,894 on p3 and a total of $196,531,806 and the FY '85 rate of $20.70 on p10, and the tax collector's commitments by levy year (p60, landed as `tax-collection`); no table by class. Searched valuation, overlay, levy and assessment (sources/data/report-tables/1984/). — closes: the Assessors' FY1985 tax rate recapitulation (Form LA-4/recap) filed with the Department of Revenue.

what: How many weighing and measuring devices did the Sealer test in 1984, and what did sealing bring in by device?
why: `report-weights-measures` holds the Sealer's device counts and fees from the 2010 report. The 1984 report prints only the receipts line `Sealing Fees` $481.00 in the statement of receipts (p43) and the voted budget line `Weights and Measures Inspector` $985 (p76); searched weights, sealer and sealing (sources/data/report-tables/1984/). — closes: the Sealer of Weights and Measures' 1984 annual report to the Division of Standards.
